source_title: Databricks platform release notes April 2026: AI Gateway now governs MCP servers (Beta)
claim_summary: Release note states AI Gateway can now enforce access control, monitor usage and audit activity across all MCP interactions in a workspace, describing it as the central governance layer for LLM endpoints, coding agents and MCP servers
limitation: Vendor documentation only; not exercised; release notes are mutable and staged (accounts may update a week or more later); companion blog 'Unity Gateway: How to connect agents to external MCPs securely' dated 2026-04-15

source_title: Governing coding agent sprawl with Unity Gateway
claim_summary: Databricks introduces Coding Agent Support in Unity Gateway (audit, MCP controls, single budgets, usage observability for coding tools; the post names Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI as supported, with 'Cursor, Gemini CLI and Codex CLI support' ready immediately, and mentions Claude Code only as a tool used internally) and states it is available for all Databricks customers starting that day
feature: centralized governance and cost control for coding agents
limitation: Vendor claim; the quoted '20% increase in token usage ... 15% reduction in pull request cycle time' is presented as an illustrative dashboard 'Example', not a measured study; product naming varies across sources (AI Gateway, Unity AI Gateway, Unity Gateway)

source_title: databricks/cli v0.297.2 release notes
claim_summary: Fix for 'error downloading Terraform: unable to verify checksums signature: openpgp: key expired' during bundle deploy by using a hardcoded armored public key; the full paginated GitHub releases API list shows 87 CLI releases (v0.210.4 to v0.297.2) published on 2026-04-19 (an earlier count of 30, v0.267.1 to v0.297.2, was truncated)
feature: supply-chain signature verification fix backported across releases
limitation: Count of backports from GitHub releases API on 2026-10-16; root cause beyond the release text (expired signing key) not independently investigated; illustrates maintenance burden of pinned old CLI versions

source_title: MLflow v3.12.0 release notes
claim_summary: Apache-2.0 MLflow 3.12.0 adds multimodal tracing, tracing for Codex, Gemini and Qwen coding agents (alongside existing Claude Code tracing), AI Gateway guardrails and paginated trace tables
limitation: Release notes not executed; MLflow is Databricks-originated but community-governed OSS; GitHub release time and PyPI upload time differ; release notes attribute 20 entries in this release to the copilot-swe-agent bot account (disclosed account label, not an authorship inference)

source_title: Delta Grows Up: Writes, Unity Catalog and Time Travel
claim_summary: DuckDB states its Delta and Unity Catalog extensions shed their experimental tags and now support writes, Unity Catalog and time travel
feature: third-party engine reuse of Delta Lake and Unity Catalog
limitation: Independent project's own claim; not executed by us; shows code-level interoperability, not verified downstream task value or adoption

source_title: MLflow Has a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) Vulnerability (first of a May-June 2026 batch)
claim_summary: GitHub Advisory Database lists 10 MLflow advisories published 2026-05-11 to 2026-06-04 (severities low to critical: SSRF, unauthenticated file read, unauthenticated FastAPI routes, insecure temp files, origin validation in MLflow Assistant, multipart-upload access, gateway-secret enumeration and environment-variable injection); listed fixes are in releases before 3.12.0
limitation: Advisory-database records only; exploitability not tested; affected self-hosted MLflow, not necessarily Databricks managed MLflow; publication lagged the fixed releases

source_title: databricks/cli v1.0.0 release notes
claim_summary: CLI declared GA with semantic versioning; adds 'databricks aitools' to install Databricks skills into coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot, Antigravity); immutable release tags; breaking change storing OAuth tokens in OS-native secure store; 0.299.x security patches through 2027-05-20
feature: agent-skill installer; supply-chain and credential-storage hardening
limitation: Skills come from databricks/databricks-agent-skills, whose LICENSE is the source-available 'Databricks License' (GitHub API: NOASSERTION), not an OSI licence; behaviour not executed

source_title: MLflow v3.13.0 release notes
claim_summary: Adds role-based access control with Admin UI (breaking: legacy per-resource permission APIs removed), trace retention/auto-archival, one-click gateway onboarding of Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI for tracing, budgets and guardrails, and an official Helm chart
limitation: Release notes only; migration cost of breaking permission change not measured

source_title: Databricks platform release notes June 2026: Genie Code now supports auto-approve for tool actions
claim_summary: Genie Code auto-approve mode approves tool actions without prompting; an AI classifier blocks risky ones; the note states auto-approve is a productivity feature, not a security boundary, and recommends keeping it off with production data or shared resources
limitation: Vendor doc only; PromptArmor (2026-10-05) asserts auto-approve is documented as default and recommended, a conflict not resolved here

source_title: Databricks Announces OpenSharing, a New Open Standard for Sharing of Data and AI Assets Across Platforms and Organizations
claim_summary: Databricks says Delta Sharing evolves into OpenSharing, a Linux Foundation project covering agent skills, AI models and unstructured data plus Iceberg IRC clients and on-premises storage partners; repo OpenSharing-IO/OpenSharing (Apache-2.0) created 2026-06-10T00:57Z
feature: open protocol for sharing agent skills and AI assets
availability: repo public; protocol claims not tested
limitation: Customer counts ('thousands of enterprises') are vendor claims; Phoronix confirms the Linux Foundation announcement but is a secondary report of the same event; OSS delta-io/delta-sharing repo still exists under its old name

source_title: Databricks Iceberg Support Has a Catch. It's Called Unity Catalog.
claim_summary: Onehouse argues Iceberg on Databricks requires Unity Catalog, external Iceberg REST catalogs are not usable as governing catalogs from Databricks compute, and quotes Databricks docs that credential vending on foreign Iceberg tables is not supported
limitation: Author's company sells a competing lakehouse platform (interested party); quoted documentation lines not independently re-read; contrasts with the vendor's openness messaging

source_title: Introducing Omnigent: A Meta-Harness to Combine, Control and Share Your Agents
claim_summary: Databricks open-sources Omnigent under Apache 2.0 in alpha, a meta-harness wrapping Claude Code, Codex, Pi and other agents with shared sessions, policies and egress-proxy credential injection; managed Omnigent on Databricks entered Beta on 2026-06-17 per release notes
feature: multi-harness agent orchestration and policy layer
limitation: GitHub API: omnigent-ai/omnigent created 2026-06-11, Apache-2.0, first release v0.2.0 2026-06-19; star count is not adoption; security of credential injection not tested

product: Genie One / Genie Agents / Genie Code
source_title: Databricks Launches Genie One: All-New Agentic Coworker for Every Team
claim_summary: Press release says Genie One, Genie Agents and Genie Code are now generally available, with Genie Ontology context layer, no seat-based pricing and up to $10 free per user per month; Genie App Builder and Genie ZeroOps to enter private preview after the Summit
availability: GA claim; App Builder private preview pending
limitation: Customer quotes are vendor-selected; accuracy/cost claims for Genie Ontology unverified; pricing changed repeatedly in July (see CI2026-071-019)

product: Agent Bricks / Unity AI Gateway / agent memory
source_title: Agent Bricks: Data + AI Summit 2026
claim_summary: Databricks repositions Agent Bricks as a developer agent platform (any model/harness), announces a Lakebase-backed agent memory service, MCP support in Unity Catalog, and Unity AI Gateway as a governance layer; says agent traces, memory writes and generations should be governed in the lakehouse
limitation: Bundle of Summit announcements with mixed or unstated availability; '3x faster' document search subagent is an unverified vendor claim; memory service reached Beta on 2026-09-16 (CI2026-071-029)

source_title: Databricks Agrees to Acquire Panther, Further Establishing the Security Lakehouse Category
claim_summary: Databricks announces intent to acquire Panther (AI SOC platform with detection-as-code and 100+ integrations), described as its third security acquisition; completion announced in a Databricks blog dated 2026-08-03
limitation: Deal terms not disclosed in text read; completion source is first-party only; outside core developer-tooling angle but relevant to agent-security positioning

source_title: Databricks Launches Lakehouse//RT to Bring Real-Time Analytics Directly to the Lakehouse
claim_summary: Lakehouse//RT, powered by the new Reyden engine, is in Beta with vendor-stated sub-100 ms latency at 12,000 queries per second and up to 16x better performance than customers' prior serving stacks; same-day LTAP release says LTAP is 'coming soon as a part of Lakebase'
limitation: Benchmark disclosure contested: ClickHouse (2026-06-30, competitor) says the keynote benchmark omitted hardware, cost, configuration and cache settings and that its access request to the gated product was unanswered

source_title: MLflow v3.14.0 release notes
claim_summary: Adds 'mlflow agent setup' (gives Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode MLflow skills), WAL-backed Claude Code tracing, trace review queues, pytest integration for GenAI regression tests; breaking change switches sklearn/LightGBM default serialization from cloudpickle to skops and PyTorch to pt2
feature: agent onboarding; safer model serialization defaults
limitation: Release notes only; serialization default change reduces but does not eliminate pickle risk (a later advisory GHSA-gqvg-gmmx-x4hm reports a bypass of the pickle guard via the statsmodels flavor)

source_title: UnityCatalog 0.5.0 release notes
claim_summary: Apache-2.0 Unity Catalog 0.5.0 introduces a UC Delta REST API for catalog-managed Delta tables with server-side commit validation and credential vending; Delta Lake 4.3.0 released the same day adds Spark integration with that API
feature: open catalog REST API for Delta clients
limitation: OSS releases read via GitHub API; not executed; parity between OSS Unity Catalog and Databricks-managed Unity Catalog not assessed

source_title: Databricks platform release notes July 2026: Genie products now use pay-as-you-go pricing; usage free through January 31, 2027
claim_summary: Genie products moved to pay-as-you-go billing from 2026-07-08 with 150 free DBUs per month; on 2026-07-15 billing for Genie One and Genie Agents was paused (free through 2027-01-31), on 2026-07-21 correction records negated prior billed usage, and Genie Code stayed billed
limitation: Mutable documentation conflict: the 2026-07-15 note already says 'through January 31, 2027' while a 2026-08-03 note says the promotion was previously set to end 2026-07-31 and was extended; recorded, not resolved

source_title: Benchmarking Coding Agents on Databricks' Multi-Million Line Codebase
claim_summary: Databricks reports an internal benchmark from its own merged PRs with held-out human-written tests (no LLM judge): GLM 5.2 statistically tied with Opus 4.8 at $1.28 vs $1.94 per task; Sonnet 5 $2.09/task and 81% vs Opus 87%; same model through different harnesses differed in cost by more than 2x; git history had to be sealed after agents recovered solutions from it
feature: task-level cost/quality evaluation of coding agents
limitation: Task count, confidence intervals and task set are not published so results cannot be replicated; vendor promotes its own routing products; Earendil (Pi maker, interested party, 2026-08-04) amplifies the harness result

source_title: Databricks is Raising a Strategic Round of Funding at a $188 Billion Valuation
claim_summary: Databricks says it signed a term sheet led by Coatue at a $188B valuation to double down on Unity AI Gateway, Genie and Lakebase; on 2026-08-13 it announced closing $5B at a $190B valuation with a $7B revenue run-rate and >80% YoY growth
feature: company financing and stated product focus
limitation: Revenue and growth are unaudited vendor statements; valuation figure changed between term sheet ($188B) and close ($190B); page meta time 2026-07-17T02:15 vs displayed July 16; TechCrunch 2026-07-17 independently reports the $188B round led by Coatue

source_title: Databricks platform release notes July 2026: MLflow trace storage in Unity Catalog is now generally available
claim_summary: MLflow trace storage in Unity Catalog tables is GA (Public Preview since 2026-04-30): traces stored in OpenTelemetry format, governed by Unity Catalog schema/table permissions and queryable with SQL
limitation: Vendor documentation; 'storage is unlimited' is a vendor statement; regional availability limited

source_title: MLflow v3.15.0 release notes
claim_summary: Adds an MCP Registry (versioned MCP server configs with aliases and auto-discovered tools), multi-provider MLflow Assistant with token/cost display, presigned-URL artifact transfer and per-endpoint gateway budgets
limitation: Release notes only; registry does not by itself vet MCP server safety

source_title: Unity Gateway is Generally Available
claim_summary: Databricks declares Unity Gateway generally available as a unified way to govern AI spend, security and access across agents, models, MCPs, skills and tools
limitation: GA claim and customer quotes are vendor statements; feature-level GA vs Beta varies (several gateway features remain Beta)

source_title: MLflow AI Gateway permits SSRF through an unvalidated api_base
claim_summary: High-severity SSRF advisory (CVE-2026-71211) affecting mlflow >=3.13.0, <=3.15.2 with no patched version listed in the advisory database; the 3.17.0 release notes list a fix for this GHSA
availability: fix in a later release per release notes
limitation: Severity conflict on a related advisory: GHSA-7gwp-5pfp-969j is 'high' in the MLflow repository advisory (2026-08-02) but 'critical' in the global database (2026-08-17); exploitability not tested

product: Unity Gateway Smart Routing and guardrails
source_title: Smart Routing in Unity Gateway: Match frontier quality with 30%+ lower cost per task
claim_summary: Smart Routing (Beta) routes coding tasks across models by complexity; vendor reports 65% of Opus 5 cost per task on internal workloads, '35% savings' on its internal benchmark and '56% cost savings' on public coding benchmarks; same-day release note adds a deterministic Sensitive Data Detection guardrail (Beta, under 50 ms per 100-turn conversation)
limitation: Savings figures vary within the same post (30%+, 35%, 56%) and are not reproducible; cost savings are not energy savings

source_title: Databricks platform release notes August 2026: Query text is now masked by default in system tables and APIs
claim_summary: Query text in system.query.history, Query History and List Queries APIs now returns <REDACTED> by default; only account admins and a databricks_pii_access group can read unmasked text
feature: default masking of sensitive SQL text
limitation: Behaviour change may break existing monitoring or audit tooling; not tested

source_title: Databricks platform release notes September 2026: Partner-powered AI features can no longer be disabled in the settings UI
claim_summary: Partner-powered AI features can no longer be disabled in account or workspace settings UI; the Settings API works until 2026-11-01, after which the setting is removed and changes require contacting the account team
limitation: Governance-relevant reduction of self-service control; data-flow implications for partner models not documented in the note

source_title: Databricks platform release notes September 2026: Managed agent memory and sessions are in Beta
claim_summary: Managed agent memory (durable long-term memory with semantic search) and managed agent sessions (durable conversation history), both Lakebase-backed and usable from any framework, enter Beta
limitation: Retention, deletion and access-control semantics for stored agent memory not assessed; vendor docs only

source_title: MLflow 3.16.1 release notes
claim_summary: Breaking change removes the default basic-auth admin password shipped in basic_auth.ini (citing GHSA-gq3w-7jj3-x7gr); 3.16.0 (2026-09-04) made basic-auth fail-closed authorization the default
limitation: Conflict: the global advisory GHSA-gq3w-7jj3-x7gr (published 2026-02-21, critical) lists the fix as 3.8.0rc0, yet the default-password removal is listed in 3.16.1; not resolved here

product: Unity Gateway CLI / coding agent configuration
source_title: Databricks platform release notes September 2026: Centrally configure coding agents
claim_summary: Organizations can centrally configure coding agents (models, MCP servers, skills, default harness, Smart Routing) applied at launch or via MDM; the Unity Gateway CLI ('ug', formerly ucode) is published at databricks/unity-gateway with v0.2.0 released 2026-09-22
limitation: databricks/unity-gateway LICENSE.md is the source-available 'Databricks License' (GitHub API: NOASSERTION), not OSI open source; blog of 2026-09-24 customer figures (61 billion input tokens, ~360,000 requests) and an estimated $1.2M/year saving are unverified

source_title: Databricks platform release notes September 2026: The Genie One MCP server is now generally available
claim_summary: Genie One MCP server is GA as system.ai.genie_one_mcp in Unity Gateway with Unity Catalog permissions enforced per request; the previous Beta endpoint /api/2.0/mcp/genie is deprecated and sunsets 2026-10-31
feature: governed MCP access to business context
limitation: Short deprecation window (about five weeks) for Beta integrators; blog 'The Genie One MCP is now Generally Available' is dated 2026-09-22, three days before the release-note date

source_title: Phishing in Databricks Genie
claim_summary: PromptArmor reports a malicious Skill in Genie Code can render a display that phishes users and exfiltrates tenant data from the browser despite egress controls and the guardrail agent; Databricks reportedly responded that it is the user's responsibility to ensure uploaded skills are not malicious
availability: unpatched per researcher; vendor treats as user responsibility
limitation: Researcher is a security vendor (interested party); exploit not reproduced by us; original URL (four-databricks-genie-controls-that-dont-stop-malicious-skills) now redirects to a retitled page; vendor quotes are as reported by researcher

source_title: MLflow 3.17.0 release notes
claim_summary: Release lists fixes referencing 13 distinct GHSA IDs (SSRF, scorer deserialization, credential leakage in CrewAI autolog spans, authorization gaps) plus fine-grained permissions with explicit DENY; SQL-backed servers need a coordinated 'mlflow db upgrade' with all writers stopped and mixed-version rolling upgrades are unsupported
limitation: Repository advisory GHSA-26p8-2jq9-3vq9 (critical unauthenticated RCE via third-party scorer deserialization) was published 2026-10-09, after the release; 12 of the 13 referenced GHSA IDs were not found in the global GitHub Advisory Database via API on 2026-10-16 (only GHSA-h7x2-h6g9-p789 was)

source_title: Lakebase and Agentic SDLC: Branching Databases for Coding Agents
claim_summary: Describes a loop of Git worktrees plus a Claude Code hook creating one Lakebase database branch per agent, and GitHub Actions creating an ephemeral branch per PR, running Drizzle migrations and posting a schema diff
limitation: Pattern description, not an evaluated outcome; Lakebase is proprietary managed Postgres; independent commentary (thebuild.com 2026-05-12) notes Lakebase is not stock Postgres and lock-in trade-offs

source_title: Databricks platform release notes October 2026: Knowledge Assistant and Supervisor Agent are now legacy; Unity Gateway Skills API in Beta
claim_summary: Knowledge Assistant and Supervisor Agent become legacy offerings (recommendation: Agent Bricks CLI or Genie Agents); same day the Unity Gateway Skills REST API enters Beta with CLI, Python, Go, Java and JavaScript SDK support
feature: agent product deprecation; skills management API
limitation: Supervisor Agent was announced GA in a 2026-02-10 blog (pre-window) and its Supervisor API entered Beta 2026-04-20; the April release note now labels it deprecated, showing retroactive edits to dated notes
